title: Closing Integral-Resistance Round Gaps for GIFT-64 and PRESENT
summary: Best known integral distinguishers reach 10 rounds for GIFT-64 and 9 for PRESENT, while resistance bounds are 12 and 13, respectively; close both gaps and explain degree extension.

formal_statement.body:
Determine whether and how the integral-resistance round bounds for the block ciphers GIFT-64 and PRESENT can be tightened to close the unresolved gaps between their best known integral distinguishers and the corresponding integral-resistance property, and explain what permits the relevant degree to be extended to more rounds.

$$\tag{S1}$$

scope.domain: Integral cryptanalysis and resistance bounds for the GIFT-64 and PRESENT block ciphers.
parameters: Round count — measures the gap between the best known integral distinguisher and the integral-resistance property for each cipher
Relevant degree — tracks extension to additional rounds
scope.unresolved_remainder: Close both cipher-specific round gaps and determine what permits the relevant degree to extend to more rounds.

citations.label: Strong and Tight Security Guarantees against Integral Distinguishers

progress.summary: The conclusion explicitly presents closing both cipher-specific gaps and gaining an intuitive understanding of degree extension as future research. The paper reports the compared round bounds without resolving the gaps.
citation_labels: Phil Hebborn et al., Strong and Tight Security Guarantees against Integral Distinguishers
